## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse consisting of 238 matching passages across 13 other Pali texts, but reports no cross-language alignments scoring 10 or higher [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Yamaka*, its highest degree of shared text occurs with other sections of the *Anusayayamaka*, notably the *Anusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.1, 56 matches) and the *Pahīnavāra* (Ya 7.2.5, 49 matches), along with analogously structured *Uppādavāra* sections across other chapters such as Ya 3.2.1, Ya 10.2.1, and Ya 6.2.1 [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (20 matches) as well as the commentary (*Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā*) and sub-commentary (*Pañcapakaraṇa-anuṭīkā*) [DharmaNexus].
